{{Short description|American ultramarathon runner}}
'''Ann Trason''' (born August 30, 1960) is an American [[ultramarathon]] runner from [[Auburn, California]].<ref name="cla"/>  She set 20 [[world record]]s during her career. Her world record of 5:40:18 at the 50 mile distance, set in 1991, was unbeaten until 2015. As of her induction into the Ultrarunning Hall of Fame in 2020, she was considered by many to be the most successful female ultrarunner of all time.<ref name="trm">{{cite news |title=Legends of the Trail |url=https://www.trailrunnermag.com/people/profiles-people/legends-of-the-trail |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=[[Trail Runner Magazine]] |date=2020-02-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IAU Records Table |url=https://iau-ultramarathon.org/assets/pdf/rankings/IAU%20Records%20Committee%202017_2020_RecordsTable_20200126.pdf |website=International Association of Ultrarunners |access-date=2 February 2021}}</ref>

==Life==

Trason was a top runner in high school, but a knee injury kept her from competing in college and injuries plagued her throughout her running career including not finishing her first two entries to the [[Western States 100]].<ref name="theg">{{cite news |last1=Homer |first1=Jill |title=Pushing through the pain: ultrarunner Ann Trason makes a quiet comeback |url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2015/feb/20/ultrarunner-anne-trason-comeback |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=the Guardian |date=2015-02-20 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="trm"/><ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.si.com/vault/1994/07/25/131694/hot-on-the-trail-ann-trason-is-amongultramarathonings-top-competitors-male-or-female | title=Hot on the Trail | author=Austin Murphy | work=[[Sports Illustrated]] | date=July 25, 1994}}</ref>

Trason's ultra career began when she entered the 1985 [[American River 50|American River 50 Miler]] at age 24<ref name="trm"/> and both won and set a course record. She returned 8 years later and dropped her time by an hour to establish the 6:09 female course record that still stands.<ref name=":0" /> Trason's Western States career began in 1987, but was not able to finish it until 1989 when she was first female finisher.<ref name="sls">{{cite web | url=https://www.therunnerstrip.com/2009/01/catching-up-with-ultra-legend-ann-trason/ | title=Catching Up with Ultra Legend Ann Trason | author=Sarah Lavender Smith | date=January 10, 2009 | accessdate=August 18, 2016}}</ref> She has won Western States 14 times, most recently in 2003.<ref name="trm"/> She held the women's course record for 18 years (17:37:51, set in 1994) until it was broken by [[Ellie Greenwood]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web | title=Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run Course Records | url=https://www.wser.org/records/ | publisher=wser.org | accessdate=August 18, 2016}}</ref>

Trason appears in [[Christopher McDougall]]'s accounts of the [[Leadville Trail 100]] in the 1990s in his 2009 book, ''Born to Run: A Hidden Tribe, Superathletes, and the Greatest Race the World Has Never Seen''. Her time of 18:06:24 in the 1994 Leadville was the women's course record until 2025.<ref>{{cite magazine | title=A Running Life: Ann Trason | author=Erin Strout | date=May 25, 2015 | work=[[Runner's World]] | url=https://www.runnersworld.com/runners-stories/a-running-life-ann-trason | accessdate=August 18, 2016}}</ref>

In both 1996 and 1997 Trason performed the "double" of winning the Western States 100 just 12 days after winning the 56-mile [[Comrades Marathon]] in South Africa.

Trason and her ex-husband and training partner Carl Andersen co-directed the Dick Collins Firetrails 50 from 2000 through 2010.<ref name="pio">{{cite news |last1=Hicks |first1=Meghan |title=Ann Trason: The Pioneer Returns |url=https://www.irunfar.com/ann-trason-the-pioneer-returns |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=iRunFar |date=2014-02-05 |language=en}}</ref> Trason set the female course record on the Firetrails 50 the one time she ran it, in 1987.<ref name="sls" />

Trason broke twenty world records during her running career in distances from forty to one hundred miles.<ref name="theg"/>

After a decade away from running once her then-husband could no longer run,<ref name="theg"/> Trason returned to the sport as crew and an occasional racer in 2013.<ref name="theg"/> She was a multi-year UltraRunner of the Year, and in 2020, she was inducted into the American Ultrarunning Hall of Fame.<ref name=":0">{{cite web | title=American Ultrarunning Hall of Fame | url=https://ultrarunninghistory.com/hall-of-fame/ | publisher=ultrarunninghistory.com | accessdate=December 23, 2020}}</ref><ref name="cla">{{cite news |last1=Pecoraro |first1=Nick |title=A class of her own: Hall of Fame comes knocking for Western States legend Trason |url=https://goldcountrymedia.com/news/187792/a-class-of-her-own-hall-of-fame-comes-knocking-for-western-states-legend-trason/ |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=goldcountrymedia.com |date=11 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="ury">{{cite web |title=UltraRunners of the year - historical |url=https://ultrarunning.com/features/reference/ultrarunners-of-the-year-historical/ |website=Ultrarunning Magazine |access-date=23 May 2021 |date=2014-12-26}}</ref>

She completed 100 miles in the 2025-2026 [[Across the Years]] ultra using her walker.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 3, 2026 |title=Ultrarunning Icon Ann Trason Reaches 100 Miles At Across The Years With A Walker |url=https://marathonhandbook.com/ultrarunning-icon-ann-trason-reaches-100-miles-at-across-the-years-with-a-walker/ |access-date=2026-01-04 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Course records==
* 5:40:18 – Houston UltraMarathon 50 mile (1991)<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 1991 |title=Houston Ultras - a Hot Day in the Sun for Ann Trason |url=https://subscriber.ultrarunning.com/archive/issue/april-1991 |website=UltraRunning Magazine}}</ref>
* 6:09:08 – [[American River 50|American River 50 mile]] (1993)
* 3:59:32 – Cool Canyon Crawl 50K (1993)
* 7:31:24 – Dick Collins Firetrails 50 mile (1987)
* 6:13:54 – Hunter Thompson 50 mile
* 18:06:24 – [[Leadville Trail 100]] women's record (2nd place overall in 1994)<ref>''Born to Run'', by Christopher McDougall. Alfred A. Knopfe, New York, 2009</ref>. This record stood until 2025 when [[Anne Flower]] broke it.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones-Wilkins |first=Andy |date=August 22, 2025 |title=Chasing Ann Trason: Anne Flower's Historic 2025 Leadville 100 Mile Run |url=https://www.irunfar.com/chasing-ann-trason-anne-flowers-2025-leadville-100-mile-course-record-run |access-date=2026-01-04 |website=iRunFar |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 8:55:49 – [[Miwok 100K Trail Race]] (2001)
* 6:43:52 – Quicksilver 50 mile (1992)
* 7:29:36 – Silver State 50 mile (1994)
